info.name: Mohammad Nasrallah — Services 4, 5, 6 (Sprint I)
info.description:
Security Incident Detection and Response Management System — Threat Intelligence (Service 4, port 8004), Security Audit Logging (Service 5, port 8005) and Security Reports (Service 6, port 8006), implemented by Mohammad Nasrallah. Every business route is prefixed with /Mohammad-Nasrallah.

Run the folders in order: authentication first, then Service 4, Service 5 and Service 6. Authentication uses Hassan Nasrallah's Service 1 on port 8000. Fill the four role passwords in the environment before running, and do not include tokens or passwords in submitted screenshots.

item.name: 0. Authentication (Mohammad Nasrallah)

request.description: Authenticate the admin account against Hassan Nasrallah's Service 1 and store the bearer token for later requests. Never include the token response in submitted evidence.
Authenticate the analyst account against Hassan Nasrallah's Service 1 and store the bearer token for later requests. Never include the token response in submitted evidence.
Authenticate the employee account against Hassan Nasrallah's Service 1 and store the bearer token for later requests. Never include the token response in submitted evidence.
Authenticate the auditor account against Hassan Nasrallah's Service 1 and store the bearer token for later requests. Never include the token response in submitted evidence.
Demonstrates failed authentication. The attempt is recorded as a "Login failed" audit record, which the activity report then counts.

item.description: Obtain bearer tokens for all four roles. Run this folder first.

item.name: 1. Service 4 — Threat Intelligence (Mohammad Nasrallah)
Add threat indicator — IP address indicator

request.description: Adds a critical malicious IP indicator. The value is validated as an IP address and stored canonically.

body.raw:
{
  "threat_type": "IP Address",
  "threat_value": "198.51.100.24",
  "description": "Command-and-control host observed in outbound beaconing",
  "severity": "Critical",
  "source": "Internal detection"
}

request.description: Adds a high-severity suspicious domain. Domain format is validated and lowercased.

body.raw:
{
  "threat_type": "Domain",
  "threat_value": "malicious-update.test",
  "description": "Phishing domain impersonating the update portal",
  "severity": "High",
  "source": "Threat feed"
}

item.name: Add threat indicator — File hash indicator

request.description: Adds a medium-severity malware hash. The digest length identifies MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 or SHA-512.

body.raw:
{
  "threat_type": "File Hash",
  "threat_value": "d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e",
  "description": "Dropper sample recovered from an email attachment",
  "severity": "Medium",
  "source": "Malware analysis"
}

request.description: The same threat type and value cannot be stored twice. A database uniqueness constraint rejects the duplicate, so concurrent requests cannot both succeed.

body.raw:
{
  "threat_type": "IP Address",
  "threat_value": "198.51.100.24",
  "description": "Command-and-control host observed in outbound beaconing",
  "severity": "Critical",
  "source": "Internal detection"
}

request.description: Returns stored indicators with their severity, source and date added, using limit/offset pagination.
Auditors hold read access to threat intelligence.
Regular employees have no access to threat intelligence APIs.
Returns the complete record for one indicator.
An unknown identifier returns 404 with the shared error shape.
Filters indicators by type. Filters combine with AND.
Filters indicators by severity level.
Value matching is a literal case-insensitive substring, so a partial indicator matches.

item.name: Search by source and type combined

request.description: Several filters narrow the result set together.
A search with no results returns an empty array rather than an error.
Analysts may search threat intelligence during investigations.
Administrators may revise the description, severity and source. Capture the record before and after this request to show the change.
Threat type and value are immutable: editing them would bypass the duplicate-indicator constraint.
An update must contain at least one non-null field.
Auditors hold read-only permissions and cannot delete threat records.
Administrators may remove a threat record.

item.description: Create, list, retrieve, search, update and delete threat indicators, including validation and authorization failures.

item.name: 2. Service 5 — Security Audit Logging (Mohammad Nasrallah)

request.description: Records a security activity. Integrating services call this endpoint with an administrator service token and the acting user in user_id.

body.raw:
{
  "user_id": "{{analyst_id}}",
  "action": "Threat indicator reviewed",
  "description": "Analyst reviewed a critical threat indicator during triage",
  "severity": "Information",
  "related_service": "Service 4: Threat Intelligence"
}

item.name: Create log record with an Idempotency-Key

request.description: Integration contract for Services 1–3 and 7–9: supplying an Idempotency-Key makes delivery retries safe. The first call creates the record.

body.raw:
{
  "user_id": "{{analyst_id}}",
  "action": "Incident assigned",
  "description": "Analyst reviewed a critical threat indicator during triage",
  "severity": "Information",
  "related_service": "Service 3: Incident Management"
}

request.description: Replaying a key returns the original record with HTTP 200 instead of creating a second row, so a teammate retry cannot duplicate the event.

body.raw:
{
  "user_id": "{{analyst_id}}",
  "action": "Incident assigned",
  "description": "Analyst reviewed a critical threat indicator during triage",
  "severity": "Information",
  "related_service": "Service 3: Incident Management"
}

item.name: Reuse the key with a different payload (rejected)

request.description: Reusing a key for a different event is a client error rather than a silent overwrite.

body.raw:

request.description: Administrators list audit records newest first. Records are produced automatically by login attempts, permission denials and data modifications across all services.
Auditors hold full read access to audit records.
Service 5's authorization table does not grant analysts the full log listing.
Regular employees have no access to audit log APIs.
Returns one audit record in full.

item.name: Retrieve a specific log as analyst

request.description: Analysts may read an individual audit record.
An unknown identifier returns 404.
Filters audit records by severity. Failed logins and permission denials are recorded as Warning.
Action matching is a literal case-insensitive substring, so this returns both successful and failed logins.

item.name: Search logs by user and date

request.description: Filters combine with AND. The date range is inclusive and interpreted in UTC.
Identifies which service produced each activity.
A search with no results returns an empty array.
Returns every activity recorded for one user, filtered on the user identifier.

exec: pm.test("all records belong to the user", () => pm.response.json().forEach(r => pm.expect(r.user_id).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("analyst_id")))));

item.name: Retrieve logs for a user with no activity

request.description: A real user with no recorded activity returns an empty array rather than an error. Run this before generating employee activity.

item.name: Retrieve logs for an unknown user

request.description: An unknown user identifier returns 404.
Analysts, auditors and employees must not delete audit records.
Auditors hold read-only permissions.
Only administrators may remove audit records. The deleted identifier, the administrator and the time are retained in an immutable deletion record.

item.description: Create, list, retrieve, search and delete audit records, retrieve logs by user, and demonstrate the idempotent ingestion contract used by teammate services.

item.name: 3. Service 6 — Security Reports (Mohammad Nasrallah)

request.description: Overall platform status: user, asset, open incident and critical threat totals. Compare these figures with the database records to verify them. The response includes a sources block naming each source service and whether the figures were collected over its API or read from the shared database.

Total incidents with distribution by severity and by lifecycle status. The response includes a sources block naming each source service and whether the figures were collected over its API or read from the shared database.

Total assets, count of critical assets and distribution by asset type. The response includes a sources block naming each source service and whether the figures were collected over its API or read from the shared database.

Threat totals grouped by severity and type, plus the most recently added indicators. The response includes a sources block naming each source service and whether the figures were collected over its API or read from the shared database.

Vulnerability totals grouped by severity and status, plus the count of critical vulnerabilities. The response includes a sources block naming each source service and whether the figures were collected over its API or read from the shared database.

Total activities, login attempts, failed login attempts and the most performed actions, derived from audit records. The response includes a sources block naming each source service and whether the figures were collected over its API or read from the shared database.
Auditors may generate every security report.
Analysts have no report generation access unless explicitly authorized.
Regular employees have no access to report APIs.

request.description: Report generation requires authentication.
